svg.aria-label: How to write ー: one unbroken stroke · 1 movement
svg.title: Writing ー
svg.desc: 1 frames; frame N shows movements 1 to N of ー (japanese), the movement being added drawn in ink over the finished letter, whose outline is read from _fonts/NotoSansJP-Subset.ttf. Stroke order after KanjiVG, kanji/030fc.svg, the long-vowel mark ー (U+30FC), one stroke path kvg:030fc-s1 (Ulrich Apel and contributors, CC BY-SA 3.0) <https://github.com/KanjiVG/kanjivg/blob/master/kanji/030fc.svg>. Source note on variation: KanjiVG stores the mark as one directed path, a bar drawn from left to right, the form it takes in horizontal writing. In vertical writing the mark turns with the line and is drawn from top to bottom; this course writes horizontally. Only the order and direction are taken from that file. The learner path's coordinates are the bundled Noto Sans JP outline's own medial line, so the print glyph's proportions, not KanjiVG's handwriting-style ones, decide where each stroke runs.
